scenarios.title: Cannot project into unsupplied area
scenarios.description: Moves cannot place pieces in a destination where they would be unsupplied, so this attempt to project is disallowed.

scenarios.title: Cannot rush into unsupplied area
scenarios.description: Moves cannot place pieces in a destination where they would be unsupplied, so this attempt to rush is disallowed.

scenarios.title: Uncommanded pieces are inactive
scenarios.description: Pieces that do not have an uninterrupted path back to their commander are not able to take actions, and so are called inactive.

scenarios.title: Rush continuation only includes pieces commanded at start of rush
scenarios.description: During a sequence of rushes, you can only act with pieces that were commanded at the start of the rush, regardless of whether will cause them to be commanded during or at the end of the sequence.

scenarios.title: Commander surrounded loss of supply
scenarios.description: When the commander no longer has a path back to their supply point, the player loses. In this case, the commander loses supply due to being surrounded by enemy players on all sides.

scenarios.title: Retreat after push
scenarios.description: When a piece is pushed, the player who owns that piece must select an adjacent destination square for the piece to retreat to.

scenarios.title: Follow after push + retreat
scenarios.description: After a player pushes a piece, and the opponent retreats the pushed piece, the player who initiated the push must "follow" the push by moving other pieces which were in the original group that initiated the push.

scenarios.title: Push with multiple follow paths
scenarios.description: Following a push, a player may have multiple ways to follow, and is free to chose either one.

scenarios.title: Imminent loss of supply due to long horizontal line
scenarios.description: The red piece at (5,3) will lose supply if blue projects to (4,2) because that will introduce new diagonal lines in addition to the long horizontal line that cuts off supply from below due to the uncommanded blue pieces at (6,0) and (6,5). This shows how uncommanded pieces can still affect opponent supply lines.

scenarios.title: Push vs. project strategy endgame
scenarios.description: This is an endgame where red has pursued a push strategy and blue, a project strategy. Both are a no more than a couple of moves away from threatening loss of supply against the opponents commander.

scenarios.title: Push group into temporarily unsupplied location
scenarios.description: Pieces can be pushed into a location where they will be temporarily unsupplied if the follow moves of the other pieces in the group will resupply the pieces.

scenarios.title: Rush chain into temporarily unsupplied location
scenarios.description: Pieces can be rushed into a location where they are temporary unsupplied if there are adjacent pieces that can be rushed in chain to resupply the pieces.

scenarios.title: Capture supply point to win by unsupplying the commander
scenarios.description: This replay ends with Player 1 capturing Player 2's supply point at (9,0), which removes Player 2's supply network and immediately wins by leaving the commander unsupplied.

scenarios.title: Commander push with no retreat
scenarios.description: This recorded game reaches a push where the blue commander has no legal retreat squares, so the commander is removed immediately and red wins the game.

scenarios.title: Rush into uncommanded location
scenarios.description: A piece can move to a location where it is no longer commanded, such as in this rush. Further moves by that piece will not be possible unless it is reconnected to its commander later on.

scenarios.title: Standard rush
scenarios.description: Example of a standard "rush" action that can kick off a rush chain

scenarios.title: Standard project
scenarios.description: Example of a standard "project" action

scenarios.title: Rush chain - can continue or end turn
scenarios.description: Now, there is a rush chain where the player can either rush other pieces which are orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to an opponent, or can end the rush chain early.

scenarios.title: Push with no retreat
scenarios.description: If a piece is pushed at a location where it cannot retreat, then it is destroyed, as will be the case after the push here.

scenarios.title: Retreat - case of only one option
scenarios.description: Following this push, the red piece must retreat to the designated square because it is the only open option.

scenarios.title: Project into uncommanded location
scenarios.description: A piece can be created in a location where it will no longer be commanded, such as in this project. Further moves by that piece will not be possible unless it is reconnected to its commander later on.

scenarios.title: Intersecting command lines cut each other off
scenarios.description: The blue and red pieces at (6,5) and (7,4) are inactive because their connection to their respective commanders has been cut off by intersecting command lines. The command lines intersect at (6,4), rendering them invalid.

scenarios.title: Short replay
scenarios.description: A legal sequence that's easy to scrub through and covers many game scenarios: Project, Destroy, Rush, Push + Retreat + Follow, etc.
